results.content:
The premise of the game was to create a live fighting game prompted by the audience. Players pick a team to join Red or Blue and then type ideas for their team’s fighter. An LLM combines multiple ideas into the next fight scene. You watch to see whether your move worked and you react in real time to the scene. You do not control each step or punch with a joystick just a prompt.

It's still very much a work in progress orchestrating and testing all the various endpoints from Gemini Flash, Fal H3 Director, Eleven Labs and Cloudflare streaming but I thought I would share what was learned so far.

results.title: AI Fighting Game Maker | Build a Brawler From a Prompt
results.content:
The part that decides whether a fighter feels good is the tuning, and that is where this pays off. Shorten the recovery on a heavy attack, add hit-stun so combos link, widen a special move's startup, give a character more health, make the impact land with a freeze frame and screen shake, all by asking. You watch each change in the running match, so dialing in how a punch feels takes minutes instead of a rebuild.

## Attacks, combos, and hit reactions you can tune [...] ## Blocking, health bars, and the best-of-three loop

A fighter is a loop, not a single exchange. The maker wires two health bars, chip damage through block, a round counter, a win-two-rounds match, and a KO with a victory pose and rematch. Ask for a stun gauge, a comeback mechanic when low on health, or a sudden-death final round and it extends the same match, so what you get is a playable game with a winner rather than two characters trading hits forever.

## 2D brawler, 3D arena, or platform fighter from one prompt box [...] ### Do I need to code to make a fighting game?

No. You can build and refine a full fighter through conversation, including the moveset, blocking, special moves, and the health and round loop. If you want to go deeper, the project uses standard scripts and scenes you can edit directly, since Summer Engine is a full game engine.

### Is the AI fighting game maker free, and can I sell what I make?

The Summer Engine desktop app is free proprietary software for local projects. Its agent tools are MIT open source. Hosted Summer AI requires an account and paid credits; signup credits are not guaranteed. You own the local project and can export and sell it without Summer royalties; each store has its own requirements.

## How the hour unfolds

The game starts with a short round in which teams estimate what AI can and can't do. Then follow several prompt rounds in which each team races against the clock to solve an assignment, from a customer email to a catchy slogan. Our game host judges the entries live on screen and keeps the scoreboard. We wrap up with a winner, a short reflection on what did and didn't work, and a few concrete tips everyone can use on Monday.

## What we arrange

We take care of the game hosting, the AI tools, all the assignments, the scoreboard and the presentation. You don't need to prepare anything yourself.

## Who is this AI teamgame for

Prompt Fight Club works best at moments when you want to wake up and engage a group in a short amount of time. Think of a Friday afternoon drink, a kick off for a new year or project, a team day, or a short block in a bigger conference programme.

You don't need any prior knowledge. The game is built for mixed groups where some people work with AI every day and others have never typed a prompt. Working in teams means one colleague lifts the other along.

## What your team learns in an hour [...] ## What your team learns in an hour

In an hour, participants discover where AI is strong and where it structurally goes wrong. They see with their own eyes the difference between a vague question and a sharp prompt, and what that difference does to the result. And they experience prompting together under time pressure, with all the outcomes live on screen so the whole room watches and laughs along.

What people take away is mostly the feeling that AI isn't magic but a tool you need to learn to steer. That's exactly the stepping stone to a properAI training.
